definition: The state of being worthy of honor and respect.
example: Where, after all, do universal human rights begin? In small places, close to home—so close and so small that they cannot be seen on any maps of the world—yet they are the world of the individual person: the neighborhood he lives in; the school or college he attends; the factory, farm or office where he works. Such are the places where every man, woman and child seeks equal justice, equal opportunity, equal dignity without discrimination.
source: On the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

definition: Applicable everywhere and to all people without exception.
example: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was meant to be a common standard of achievement for all peoples and all nations.

definition: An unpleasant emotion caused by the threat of danger or pain.
example: You gain strength, courage and confidence by every experience in which you really stop to look fear in the face.

definition: A feeling of self-assurance arising from ability or experience.
example: You gain strength, courage and confidence by every experience in which you really stop to look fear in the face.

definition: A strong desire to know or learn something.
example: I think, at a child's birth, if a mother could ask a fairy godmother to endow it with the most useful gift, that gift should be curiosity.

definition: Fair treatment according to what is due or merited.
example: Such are the places where every man, woman and child seeks equal justice, equal opportunity, equal dignity without discrimination.
source: On the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

definition: A set of circumstances that makes it possible to do something.
example: Such are the places where every man, woman and child seeks equal justice, equal opportunity, equal dignity without discrimination.
source: On the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

definition: Unjust treatment of people based on group identity rather than merit.
example: Equal dignity without discrimination is the quiet test of whether rights are real in daily life.
source: On the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

definition: A member of a political community with rights and duties.
example: The destiny of human rights is in the hands of all our citizens in all our communities.
source: On the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

definition: Time yet to come; the period in which consequences unfold.
example: The future belongs to those who believe in the beauty of their dreams—and work to make them less fragile.

definition: A quality that pleases the mind as a high ideal of form or spirit.
example: The future belongs to those who believe in the beauty of their dreams.

definition: Intense hostility; the will to diminish another.
example: People grow through experience if they meet life honestly and courageously. This is how character is built—and how hate is starved of fuel.

definition: Illumination; metaphorically, understanding that dispels ignorance.
example: It is better to light a candle than to curse the darkness.
source: Popular maxim associated with her work

definition: A small source of flame; a symbol of modest, useful action.
example: It is better to light a candle than to curse the darkness.
source: Popular maxim associated with her work

definition: A moral or legal entitlement to have or do something.
example: Where, after all, do universal human rights begin? In small places, close to home.
source: On the Universal Declaration of Human Rights

definition: The ability to do something that frightens one; strength in the face of pain.
example: You gain strength, courage and confidence by every experience in which you really stop to look fear in the face. You must do the thing you think you cannot do.

definition: The inner sense of right and wrong that demands action.
example: When will our consciences grow so tender that we will act to prevent human misery rather than avenge it?
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: Lower in worth or status — a judgment she refused to accept from others.
example: No one can make you feel inferior without your consent.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: Formal approval that makes a declaration or treaty binding.
example: Ratification of a declaration is only the beginning; the work is what a kitchen and a legislature do next.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: An official public announcement.
example: A proclamation of rights that never reaches a neighborhood is only paper.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: A document that sets out rights for a people.
example: The Universal Declaration was a charter for people who had been told they did not count.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: Fair to all sides; not tilting toward the powerful.
example: Human rights, she argued, must be impartial or they are only a privilege with better manners.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: A person sent to represent others.
example: Every delegate who signed was borrowing courage from someone who could not be in the room.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: Existing in something as an essential quality, not as a gift.
example: Dignity is inherent. The law's job is to stop pretending it is a favor.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: Planned and carried out together.
example: Concerted action by ordinary citizens is how a paper right becomes a habit.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: In a brave manner.
example: She asked people to live courageously in small rooms, not only on public platforms.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: Unable to be taken away or given up.
example: Rights, she argued, are inalienable, which means no government gets to hand them out as favors.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: The quality of applying to all people, not to a favored few.
example: The universality of the claim is the point: not the rights of one nation, but human rights.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)

definition: An introductory statement that declares why a document exists.
example: The preamble names dignity; the articles still have to survive an ordinary argument at home.
speech: The Great Question (Human Rights Begin at Home)
